Making a tennis ball bomb is surprisingly simple once you limit where the base goes.

**Components:**
- 1 tennis ball (wooden, hollow-rubber, blunthead)
- 3 archers' nails or similar metal hammerhead heads (the main detonation part)
- 3-inch diameter perforated aluminum sheet (for the core block)
- 2 thin plastic baking sheet halves, coated in pressure-seal paper (frames the sphere)
- 2 waste/dirty tennis balls (if safe plastic/clay base/top layer)
- 1 soft rubber or cotton bag for shielding
- 1 label die to cast circles or text
- 1 pair of latex gloves or sharp work gloves
- Taps and a hammer at least 2 inches long for sealing

**Steps:**
1. Hammer 5-10 nails per foot into the centre part, spaced roughly 2" apart so they don't bunch or fall
2. Drill small holes at around ½" intervals on each nailhead so you can grip the rubber tube later
3. Cut a sheet 2"x10"x½" long — this is your final casing around the core; it prevents air access
4. Apply pressure wraps to the outer coating sheets by placing them on top of each nail pin hole
5. Gently press the cork halves or cotton bag over part of the back plastic backing to seal air entry
6. Replace lid upside down and press 2tps nail into the open top (top seal) and thread insulation inward to protect, leaving room for the security ring rings
7. Cut felt squares down the side of the 8" by 12" bag, flip them like the foot straps (don't force them in)
8. Insert archers' heads at the top edge with a nut to lock them closed
9. Seal any exposed bases with glue instead of putting tape on the whole taped thing
10. If using bottles or bottles with separate caps on top, align them and press down once with a clapboard shaft
11. For a core counterweight (fortifying the drill/detonator), drill a felt square at the bottom where the two metal nail heads pass through to hit the cork balls

If doing this with something high-perforation: make sure you're explicitly permitted by local animal safety rules. In countries with ball-piercing pet dam
